`readreq` separates release selection, asset download, parsing and analysis.
This makes it possible to retrieve an exact edition once, record its source
hashes, and replay the parsed result without live network access.

## Choose a cache

`req_cache_dir()` returns the platform-appropriate user cache location using
`tools::R_user_dir("readreq", "cache")`. For a vignette, use a temporary
directory so that rendering is isolated and leaves no project or home files.

```{r cache-location}
library(readreq)

req_cache_dir()

cache_dir <- tempfile("readreq-offline-cache-")
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Raw assets are content-addressed and immutable. Parsed artifacts include the
release or local input identity, source hash, parser version and selection;
current-view artifacts additionally include the view policy. Re-fetching or
reparsing a requested asset does not delete an existing raw snapshot. Cache storage can
therefore grow over time: `readreq` has no automatic pruning or cleanup API.
Use a caller-selected temporary or project cache when appropriate, and remove
only that path manually after confirming that no read or download is using it.
Do not delete a shared/default cache while another process may hold a lock or
be replaying an artifact.

Workbook parsing defaults to one worker (`getOption("readreq.workers", 1L)`).
Leave that default in portable workflows; if a caller explicitly opts into
parallel parsing on a platform that supports it, configure no more than two
workers and account for the additional memory use.

## Replay a local input

The same cache contract applies to a local workbook. The second read below
returns the same object from the parsed cache and does not need a network
request.

```{r offline-replay}
forecast_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx", package = "readreq"
)
if (!nzchar(forecast_path)) {
  forecast_path <- file.path(
    "..", "inst", "extdata", "readreq-example-forecast.xlsx"
  )
}
stopifnot(nzchar(forecast_path), file.exists(forecast_path))

first <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path, view = "canonical", cache_dir = cache_dir
)
second <- read_req_forecasts(
  forecast_path, view = "canonical", cache_dir = cache_dir
)

stopifnot(identical(first, second))
c(rows = nrow(second), parsed_cache_files = length(list.files(
  cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, all.files = FALSE
)))
```

An exact cached release can be read offline after all requested assets have
been retrieved. A partial cache cannot satisfy a request for a missing asset;
the package reports a typed asset or download failure instead of returning an
incomplete release. Keep the exact `release_id`, package version, source
hashes and parser version with downstream outputs.

## Network and credentials

For catalogue release IDs, source assets are requested from the bundled HTTPS
URLs. A supplied one-row manifest or custom transport can use another
controlled source. No REQ data-source credential, API token or browser session
is required by the default transport. `"latest"` is a
convenience selector and can change when an installed package/catalogue update
adds a newer edition; use an
exact ID such as `"req-2026-06"` for a pinned analysis. Downloads use bounded
timeouts and retries, and the default tests and vignettes are offline.

The following is the only live call in this article. It is opt-in so that
CRAN checks, offline builds and ordinary vignette rendering never contact the
source site. It is illustrative rather than required for the offline path.

```{r live-download}
if (identical(Sys.getenv("READREQ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  live_cache <- tempfile("readreq-live-cache-")
  download_req_release(
    "req-2026-06",
    assets = c("forecast", "historical"),
    cache_dir = live_cache
  )
}
```

Official workbooks and reports are not bundled by this package. Source rights
and exclusions can differ by edition; consult the exact release terms and
`req_attribution()` before sharing source-derived material. Synthetic example
workbooks are reduced and derived fixtures and are not official data.
